title: Generating Images and Video · Level 1
slo: Describe how diffusion generates an image from a written prompt.

exercises.question_text: Which actions happen during diffusion iterations? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Each iteration removes more noise. This gradually clarifies the image.
Noise removal allows structure to emerge. The scene becomes progressively clearer.
Assigning labels prepares supervised training data. It is not a diffusion-generation action.
options.better_fit: Use it when preparing labeled training data.

options.rationale: Drawing bounding boxes is associated with object detection. Diffusion iterations develop generated structure.
options.better_fit: Use it when locating objects in an image.

exercises.question_text: What creates a new image from a written description?

options.rationale: Image generation creates new visual content from written descriptions. It relates language to visual features.
Contextual image analysis interprets an existing image. It does not create a new image from words.
options.better_fit: Use it to describe or infer context from an existing image.

options.rationale: Object detection locates known objects in an existing image. It does not synthesize a new scene.
options.better_fit: Use it to identify and locate objects in an image.

options.rationale: Image classification assigns labels to an existing image. It does not generate visual content.
options.better_fit: Use it to predict an image category.

exercises.question_text: Diffusion creates its final image in one step, without evaluating it against the prompt.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The iterative process would be omitted.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Diffusion repeatedly removes noise and evaluates the developing image against the prompt.

exercises.question_text: Image synthesis can generate an image or video from a description of desired visual content.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Image synthesis generates requested images or video from descriptions.

exercises.question_text: What must video generation account for? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Video generation must account for physical behavior. A walking dog's feet should stay on the ground.
Temporal progression requires events to unfold logically over time. Video needs coherent event order.
A video contains moving content over time. One still image has no temporal progression.
options.better_fit: Use a still image when generating one fixed visual.

options.rationale: Bounding boxes can describe object locations but do not ensure physical or temporal coherence. Video generation must model motion over time.
options.better_fit: Use bounding boxes for object-detection results.

exercises.question_text: What technique transforms random pixel noise into an image that matches a prompt?

options.rationale: Diffusion transforms random pixel noise into a prompt-matching image. It works iteratively.
Convolutional filtering applies kernels to an image. It does not generate a scene from noise.
options.better_fit: Use it to blur, sharpen, or highlight edges.

options.rationale: Object detection identifies objects in an existing image. It does not synthesize a prompt-matching image.
options.better_fit: Use it to locate objects in an image.

options.rationale: Image classification predicts a label for an image. It does not transform noise into a scene.
options.better_fit: Use it to assign a category to an image.

exercises.question_text: Video generation can ignore the order of events over time as long as each frame looks realistic.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The clip could become logically incoherent.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Video generation requires temporal progression as well as realistic-looking frames.

exercises.question_text: In diffusion, a prompt helps identify related visual features that can be combined into an image.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The prompt's role would be missed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The prompt identifies visual features for the requested image.

exercises.question_text: What should the final result show for the prompt “A dog carrying a stick in its mouth”?

options.rationale: The prompt requests a dog carrying a stick. The generated result can depict that scene.
A class label names an image subject. It does not depict the requested scene.

options.text: A bounding box around a dog
options.rationale: A bounding box gives a location for a detected dog. It does not show the requested dog-and-stick scene.

options.text: A pixel mask of a dog
options.rationale: A pixel mask identifies a region in an image. It is not a generated depiction of the requested scene.

exercises.question_text: What can a prompt do for an image-generation model? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A prompt describes desired visual content. It tells the model what should appear.
Prompts guide desired visual features. Those features shape the result.

options.text: Label every pixel in a photo.
options.rationale: Pixel labeling is semantic segmentation. A prompt is written guidance.
options.better_fit: Use semantic segmentation to label pixels in a photo.

options.rationale: Bounding-box coordinates are detection results. They are not natural-language generation guidance.
options.better_fit: Use bounding-box coordinates to report an object's location.

exercises.question_text: For a dog-and-stick prompt, intermediate diffusion results progressively form the requested scene from noise.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The gradual formation of the scene would be missed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Diffusion produces increasingly structured intermediate results from noise.

exercises.question_text: A prompt is a set of random pixel values used to start an image.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The prompt would be confused with the noisy starting state.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A prompt is natural-language guidance; diffusion starts with random pixel values.

flashcards.back: Generating an image or video from a description of desired visual content.
A natural-language description that guides desired visual features.
flashcards.hint: It tells the model what to create.

flashcards.back: A technique that transforms random pixel noise into a prompt-matching image.
Events unfolding in a logical sequence over time.
